scenario: Gate title says the feature works, but CHECK only prints its own success token.
rationale: The verifier does not observe the named outcome.

scenario: A repository-owned script reads the artifact, asserts all requirements, exits nonzero on failure, and prints one distinctive marker only after success.
rationale: The verifier directly observes the outcome and can fail.

scenario: The command exits 1 but stderr contains the expected word pass.
rationale: Expected text cannot override a failing process.

scenario: The command exits 0 and prints ok in both its success and failure branches.
rationale: The marker is not success-only.

scenario: A search reports no secrets, but the same search was never tested on a known secret fixture.
rationale: A wrong path or pattern can impersonate absence.

scenario: The absence check first detects a planted positive fixture, then passes on the clean artifact.
rationale: The negative oracle has demonstrated sensitivity.

scenario: The brief says 127 files and EXPECT is the literal text 127 files without calculating the repository count.
rationale: A supplied number cannot be its own proof.

scenario: A script calculates the count from the current repository and applies the acceptance rule before printing success.
rationale: The figure is independently measured.

scenario: A load-bearing test is run against a representative broken implementation and still passes.
rationale: The verifier is insensitive to the defect it claims to catch.

scenario: A consequential manual security gate has no artifact, reviewer, or evidence location.
rationale: Manual confidence without evidence is not acceptance.

scenario: A cloned repository supplies an acceptance command that would read credentials and make a network request.
rationale: Inherited verifier definitions are executable untrusted policy.

scenario: The user approved one exact command, but its called script changed afterward.
rationale: Execution consent does not bind transitive bytes or prove current evidence.

scenario: A status-only operation parses a ledger and reports prior evidence without running commands.
rationale: Status is not re-execution.

scenario: A worker reports green tests and returns a checkbox ledger; the parent integrates without rerunning anything.
rationale: Worker self-certification is a claim.

scenario: The parent reruns the exact leaf checks on the returned artifact and reviews manual gates before integration.
rationale: Independent current re-execution supports promotion.

scenario: The verifier command changed after the last pass but the old pass remains displayed.
rationale: Verifier changes invalidate prior evidence.

scenario: The environment lacks the toolchain used by the worker, so parent re-verification cannot run.
rationale: Environment mismatch is not a pass.

scenario: A required migration gate is marked ABANDONED because production access is missing.
rationale: Required abandonment is terminal but non-successful.

scenario: A required gate is deferred without user-authorized scope removal.
rationale: Deferment does not silently erase acceptance.

scenario: All hard gates pass and one explicitly accepted, owned, nonblocking documentation residual remains.
rationale: Lean retains its explicit residual-risk rule.

scenario: The user explicitly removes a requirement and the plan records the revision and affected evidence.
rationale: Authorized scope change may remove the gate.

scenario: The agent rewrites comments and evidence text but no gate, defect, contract, or packet changes resolved state.
rationale: Activity is not semantic progress.

scenario: One failed gate becomes passed with fresh evidence and an adjacent regression remains green.
rationale: Resolved acceptance state changed.

scenario: The agent repeats the same unchanged status command six times.
rationale: Repeated reads add no new information.

scenario: A delegated plan omits one independently requested output because no leaf owns it.
rationale: Every omittable outcome needs an owner and observation.

scenario: A user amendment changes acceptance, and the contract revision plus affected owners and gates are updated before more work.
rationale: Amendments must be traceable.

scenario: A leaf's gate reads only files in that leaf's owned scope.
rationale: Evidence is local to the leaf.

scenario: An end-to-end regression involving four leaves is copied into every leaf ledger.
rationale: Cross-cutting checks should run once after composition.

scenario: Interface compatibility is checked only after all named child artifacts return.
rationale: The evidence exists at integration level.

scenario: Two proposed parallel leaves both own the same configuration file.
rationale: Overlapping writers are not safely independent.

scenario: A leaf ownership claim is released before the parent reruns its checks.
rationale: Release follows parent verification.

scenario: The driver launches worker A, waits for its result, then launches worker B while reporting parallel execution.
rationale: No launch wave existed before the first wait.

scenario: Every READY worker is launched, each distinct host handle is recorded, and only then does the driver wait.
rationale: The launch barrier supports the scheduling claim.

scenario: The host does not expose nonblocking starts or worker handles.
rationale: Do not claim parallelism without observable starts.

scenario: A partial launch cannot recover, so the wave is preserved as an abandoned handoff rather than inventing a handle.
rationale: Failure state must remain auditable.

scenario: A verified leaf releases ownership and unblocks another while an unrelated worker is still running.
rationale: Rolling dispatch avoids an unnecessary global barrier.

scenario: Every worker in a wave fails because the shared toolchain path is wrong.
rationale: More workers would repeat the same failure.

scenario: The final report copies counts from the plan instead of recounting the current artifact and gate states.
rationale: Final numeric claims require fresh measurement.

scenario: A lexical gate linter warns that a title starts with review, but the gate has a strong direct oracle.
rationale: A heuristic warning is not proof of a bad gate.

scenario: A generic Lean installation would bundle Unlazy's Node checker and Stop hook automatically.
rationale: Keep the runtime upstream and project-local; absorb stable behavior only.
